Olivia (PM): Quick sync — we need a narrow decision set for the next sprint on model lifecycle: onboarding gates, benchmark pass/fail thresholds, default pin TTLs, and deprecation guardrails. I sketched a proposal below, want feedback before we turn into RFC.

Olivia (PM): Proposed decision points:
- Acceptance metrics: accuracy delta <= 2% vs baseline on tenant prompt set, embedding cosine >= 0.98 for stable pairs, and freshness regression <= 1%
- Perf gates: p50 latency < 120ms, p95 < 450ms under canary load
- Pin TTL: default 30d, auto-unpin after 90d unless customer opts-in
- Deprecation windows: 30d customer notice + 60d migration runway for enterprise tiers
- Escape hatch: manual pin extension + rollback-credit pot for customers migrating off platform-specific shims

Jake (Eng Runtime): LGTM overall. A few notes:
- p95 450ms depends a lot on sequence length distribution; we should make gates sequence-aware (short/med/long lanes).
- "auto-unpin" needs a safety: if a customer has active traffic in last 7d we shouldn't auto-unpin.
- We can implement a "pin-extension" API for CS to grant 1-off 30d extends.

Maria (Applied ML): On the evaluation side:
- Want to pin down a canonical prompt harness per model family. Random tenant sampling + top-100 tenant prompts for regression checks.
- Recommend adding semantic shift detection: if embeddings drift > 0.015 average cosine on the probe set, flag for human review.
- For embeddings stability, also track median distance not just mean.

Sam (Eng Infra): Ops implications:
- Canary lanes: we need two canaries: internal synthetic + 3 live-customer cohorts (low, med, high qps). That lets us catch perf regressions tied to traffic shape.
- Automate rollout rollback: if p95 or error-rate exceed threshold for >3 consecutive minutes in any canary, auto-fallback to previous model.
- Pin TTL enforcement: we can implement a scheduled job that emits warnings to customer and CS 14d/3d before auto-unpin.

Alex (Customer Success): Customers asking for longer TTLs (esp regulated customers). Common asks: 6 months pinned for auditability. Can we add a contract clause for enterprise pin exceptions?

Natalie (Legal): We can add a contract addendum for extended pin windows but need to couple with acceptance gates and a migration plan. Also: retention of model artifacts for audits — define TTL and export process.

Olivia (PM): Proposal update after comments:
- Make pin TTL default 30d, but "enterprise-exception" available in contract for 180d with migration credits required.
- Add sequence-lane perf gates (short/med/long).
- Canary policy + auto-fallback as Sam suggested.
- Add embedding drift alert threshold and median-based stability metric.

Jake (Eng Runtime): Question: how strict are we on the accuracy delta? 2% vs baseline can be noisy for small sample tenants. Suggest we use a hybrid: absolute delta for high-volume tenants, and a t-test-ish threshold for low-volume tenants (or require additional human signoff).

Maria (Applied ML): Agree with hybrid approach. Also recommend running a small multi-round A/B sample for generations (n=3 seeds) to estimate variability.

Alex (Customer Success): Operational ask: expose a self-serve "request pin extension" UI for customers and surface the audit trail to CS. That reduces manual churn.

Sam (Eng Infra): Implementation note: we'll need a new ACL for request approvals and a runbook for when manual rollback is triggered. I'll draft canary SLA triggers and the job for pre-unpin warnings.

Natalie (Legal): For the contract language I'll draft a standard "pin exception addendum" and a migration-credit definition. Will sync with Alex for customer wording.

Olivia (PM): Next steps:
- Jake + Sam: prototype canary policy + auto-fallback (1 sprint)
- Maria: deliver canonical prompt harness and drift probes (1 sprint)
